study_title.title: Study Title
study_title.value: A Phase 2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of the Safety of Ritonavir-Boosted GS-9137 (GS-9137/r) Administered in Combination With Other Antiretroviral Agents for the Treatment of HIV-1 Infected Subjects

operational_feasibility.title: Operational Feasibility
operational_feasibility.value: 70/100 (Enrollment: 25/25, Site Diversity: 20/25, Patient Retention: 5/25, Timeline Adherence: 20/25)

differentiation_index.title: Differentiation Index
differentiation_index.value: 65/100 (Novelty of MoA: 20/25, Patient Population: 15/25, Dosing Regimen: 15/25, Endpoint Selection: 15/25)

value.description: Elvitegravir (EVG) 85 mg or 150 mg tablet boosted with Ritonavir (RTV) 100 mg capsule, administered orally once daily with food in combination with an investigator-selected antiretroviral (ARV) regimen.

value.exclusion: Females who are pregnant or breastfeeding. Participation in any other clinical trial without prior approval from the Sponsor. Any other clinical condition or prior therapy that, in the opinion of the investigator, would make the subject unsuitable for the study. Subjects receiving ongoing therapy with contraindicated drugs.
value.inclusion: Completion of a prior EVG+RTV treatment study without treatment-limiting toxicity. Males and females of childbearing potential must agree to utilize effective contraception methods. Ability to understand and sign a written informed consent form.

value.description: This is a single-arm, open-label study.

primary_endpoint.title: Primary Endpoint
primary_endpoint.value: Percentage of Participants Experiencing Any Treatment-Emergent Study Drug-Related Adverse Event

patient_segment.title: Patient Segment
patient_segment.value: HIV-1 infected participants who have completed a prior EVG+RTV treatment study and require continued access to the treatment for long-term safety observation.

regulatory_risk.title: Regulatory / Commercial Risks
value: Difficulty in demonstrating efficacy and safety against current standard of care due to the single-arm, open-label design.
Emergence of unexpected long-term adverse events could impact the drug's safety profile.
The long duration of the study (8 years) means the treatment landscape for HIV may have evolved, potentially making the findings less relevant.
Lack of a comparator arm makes it challenging to attribute adverse events directly to the study drug.

execution_risk.title: Execution Risks
value: Extremely high dropout rate (62%) compromises the integrity and interpretability of long-term safety and efficacy data.
Maintaining patient adherence and engagement over a very long follow-up period (up to 408 weeks) is challenging.
Managing a large number of sites (50) increases logistical complexity and potential for site-to-site variability.
Ensuring consistent data collection and reporting across all sites over nearly a decade can lead to data quality issues.

strategic_options.title: Strategic Options
value: Implement robust patient retention strategies in future long-term studies to mitigate high dropout rates.
Utilize real-world evidence or synthetic control arms to provide comparative context for the single-arm data for regulatory discussions.
Conduct subgroup analyses to identify patient populations that may have a more favorable risk/benefit profile.
Focus on the unique long-term safety data as a key differentiator, assuming no major safety signals arise.

value.schedule: Administered orally once daily with food
